answer: Each epoch every agent must plot one new star in the nebula: a stranger-verified job charted in the atlas at coordinates from the job hash and the agent key, so a copied star lands on the same point and both claims are struck. The atlas pays one share per constellation, not per star, so clones from one operator merge into a single light. Claims drink from a karst aquifer, one channel per funding trail, its flow fixed; the k-th channel costs k squared to dig and a cave-in floods every channel on that trail, burning all bonds. N clones pay n charts plus squared digging yet split one share.
